title: Normalized derived constant/stalk equivalence at a geometric point
statement: Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and $S:\operatorname{Ab}(s_{\mathrm{Et}})\to\operatorname{Ab}$ the geometric stalk at the identity geometric point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Let $C_s:\operatorname{Ab}\to\operatorname{Ab}(s_{\mathrm{Et}})$ be the constant-sheaf functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. These are exact quasi-inverse additive equivalences. The canonical constant-germ maps $N\to S C_sN$ are the unit isomorphisms; the counit $C_s S G\to G$ is the unique map whose image under $S$ is the inverse of that unit at $SG$. Applying these functors termwise gives quasi-inverse equivalences $S_D:D(s_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)\rightleftarrows D(\mathbf Z):C_s$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], preserving every cohomological lower bound. These are symmetric monoidal for ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]: their tensor comparisons are the derived canonical germ and constant-sheaf comparisons, normalized on constant sections by $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$, and the displayed unit and counit are monoidal natural isomorphisms.

proof.text: The adopted source theorem Scheme.isEquivalence_constantSheaf_of_isSepClosed proves that the actual constant-sheaf functor is an equivalence. Compose its counit with the canonical constant-germ isomorphism to identify the actual stalk with its inverse. Full faithfulness of the stalk then constructs the unique counit having inverse germ as its stalk. Naturality of the germ and cancellation prove both triangle identities.

The canonical constant-presheaf/fiber isomorphism is monoidal: evaluate at each colimit insertion, where the tensor formula is the identity on pure tensors. The sheafification/fiber comparison is already monoidal; compose the two squares to prove monoidality of the constant-germ unit. The unit tensor equation and triangle identity prove that this adjunction is monoidal, hence its counit is monoidal.

Apply the proved abstract exact monoidal adjoint-equivalence descent lemma. This supplies the strong structures on the actual mapDerivedCategory functors, both prescribed localization-factor comparisons, and the monoidal descended unit and counit. Invertibility follows from the exact adjunction API. The exact-functor cohomology comparison preserves every lower bound.

The Koszul symmetry on complexes squares to the identity, since the two signs multiply to one. The same equality passes through homotopy and the derived bifunctor universal property, producing the canonical integer derived symmetric braiding. Pull back this symmetry along the fully faithful strong derived stalk. Its compatibility is definitional; the monoidal derived unit identifies the composite constant/stalk functor with the identity, and faithfulness of the stalk proves the constant symmetry equation.
